config.title: Hohenschönhausen - FAQ
config.subtitle: How to actually get into the former Stasi remand prison in Lichtenberg: the English tour times, what it costs, how long it takes, which tram stop to use, and which station to ignore.

items.q: Can you visit Hohenschönhausen without a guided tour?
items.a: **No. The former prison can only be seen as part of a guided tour.** The memorial is open daily from 10:00 to 18:00 and the permanent exhibitions in the front building are free to visit on your own, but the cells, corridors and interrogation rooms are only opened with a guide.

items.q: What time are the English tours at Hohenschönhausen?
items.a: **English guided tours run daily at 10:40, 12:40 and 14:40.** German tours run more often, and there are specialised German tours on set weekdays. Check the memorial's own tour page shortly before you travel, because seasonal and special tours shift around the standard slots.

items.q: How much does a Hohenschönhausen tour cost?
items.a: **9 euro standard, 5 euro concession and 2.50 euro for school pupils.** A booked group tour of up to 25 people is a 110 euro flat rate, 90 euro concession and 60 euro for students. The exhibitions themselves are free.

items.q: How long should I allow for the visit?
items.a: **About 2 hours for the tour itself, including a short introductory film.** Add the travel: roughly 33 minutes each way from Alexanderplatz and about 50 minutes from Zoologischer Garten. Taking the 10:40 tour from Alexanderplatz means leaving around 09:52 and being back in the centre around 13:13.

items.q: Do I need to book a Hohenschönhausen tour in advance?
items.a: **Booking is strongly recommended for individuals and required for groups of seven or more.** Each tour is limited to 25 participants, so a full slot is a real possibility. Individual visitors book through the memorial's ticket shop.

items.q: How do I get to Hohenschönhausen memorial by public transport?
items.a: **Take the M5 tram and get off at Freienwalder Str.**, then walk about 570 metres to Genslerstraße 66. The M5 runs direct from Hackescher Markt and Alexanderplatz with no changes. Bus 256 to Große-Leege-Str./Freienwalder Str. leaves the shortest walk, about 280 metres. The whole trip is inside fare zone AB.

items.q: Why should I not take the S-Bahn to Hohenschönhausen?
items.a: **Because S Hohenschönhausen station is about 2.8 kilometres from the memorial.** It carries the district name, not the address, and the memorial's own directions tell visitors not to use it. The tram stop called Genslerstr. is a milder version of the same trap: it shares the street name but sits about 850 metres from number 66, so stay on the M5 one more stop.

**The memorial recommends the visit for ages 14 and over.** The tours are led by former prisoners of the building and by historians, and they do not soften what happened in the cells and interrogation rooms. Photography for private use is permitted during the tour.

items.q: What is the U-Boot at Hohenschönhausen?
items.a: **It is the underground cellar prison, nicknamed the submarine by the people held in it.** The Soviet secret service opened the basement of the former kitchen building as a remand prison in 1947 and handed it to the Stasi in 1951. The Stasi built the newer prison above ground in 1960 and used it as its central remand prison for political prisoners until 1989.

items.q: What should I do after visiting Hohenschönhausen?
items.a: **Keep the rest of the day light.** The visit is heavy and stacking a second memorial on the same afternoon rarely works. A walk, the Ringbahn or a coffee in Prenzlauer Berg on the way back is a better pairing. If Cold War Berlin is your theme, save the Stasi Museum in Lichtenberg for a different day.
